1→# Getting Started: Your First Plugin
     2→
     3→This tutorial walks you through creating, developing, testing, and publishing an OpenACP plugin from scratch. No prior knowledge of OpenACP internals is required.
     4→
     5→---
     6→
     7→## Prerequisites
     8→
     9→- **Node.js** 18+ installed
    10→- **npm** or **pnpm** installed
    11→- **OpenACP** installed globally (`npm install -g @openacp/cli`)
    12→- A working OpenACP setup (run `openacp onboard` if you haven't yet)
    13→
    14→---
    15→
    16→## Step 1: Scaffold a New Plugin
    17→
    18→Run the scaffold command:
    19→
    20→```bash
    21→openacp plugin create
    22→```
    23→
    24→You will be prompted for:
    25→
    26→```
    27→◆  Create a new OpenACP plugin
    28→│
    29→◇  Plugin name (e.g., @myorg/adapter-matrix)
    30→│  @myorg/hello-world
    31→│
    32→◇  Description
    33→│  A greeting plugin for OpenACP
    34→│
    35→◇  Author
    36→│  Your Name <you@example.com>
    37→│
    38→◇  License
    39→│  MIT
    40→│
    41→◆  Plugin scaffolded!
    42→│
    43→│  Next steps
    44→│
    45→│  cd hello-world
    46→│  npm install
    47→│  npm run build
    48→│  npm test
    49→│
    50→│  # Start development with hot-reload:
    51→│  openacp dev .
    52→│
    53→└  Plugin @myorg/hello-world created in ./hello-world
    54→```
    55→
    56→The scaffold creates a directory named after your plugin (without the scope prefix):
    57→
    58→```
    59→hello-world/
    60→  src/
    61→    index.ts                  # Plugin entry point
    62→    __tests__/
    63→      index.test.ts           # Test file
    64→  package.json
    65→  tsconfig.json
    66→  .gitignore
    67→  .npmignore
    68→  .editorconfig
    69→  README.md
    70→```
    71→
    72→---
    73→
    74→## Step 2: Explore the Template
    75→
    76→### package.json
    77→
    78→Key fields in the generated `package.json`:
    79→
    80→```json
    81→{
    82→  "name": "@myorg/hello-world",
    83→  "version": "0.1.0",
    84→  "type": "module",
    85→  "main": "dist/index.js",
    86→  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
    87→  "scripts": {
    88→    "build": "tsc",
    89→    "dev": "tsc --watch",
    90→    "test": "vitest",
    91→    "prepublishOnly": "npm run build"
    92→  },
    93→  "peerDependencies": {
    94→    "@openacp/plugin-sdk": "^1.0.0"
    95→  },
    96→  "devDependencies": {
    97→    "@openacp/plugin-sdk": "^1.0.0",
    98→    "typescript": "^5.4.0",
    99→    "vitest": "^3.0.0"
   100→  }
   101→}
   102→```
   103→
   104→The `@openacp/plugin-sdk` package provides all types, base classes, and testing utilities you need.
   105→
   106→### src/index.ts
   107→
   108→The generated entry point contains every lifecycle hook with inline documentation:
   109→
   110→```typescript
   111→import type { OpenACPPlugin, PluginContext, InstallContext, MigrateContext } from '@openacp/plugin-sdk'
   112→
   113→const plugin: OpenACPPlugin = {
   114→  name: '@myorg/hello-world',
   115→  version: '0.1.0',
   116→  description: 'A greeting plugin for OpenACP',
   117→
   118→  permissions: ['events:read', 'services:register'],
   119→
   120→  async setup(ctx: PluginContext): Promise<void> {
   121→    // Called during server startup. Register services, commands, middleware here.
   122→  },
   123→
   124→  async teardown(): Promise<void> {
   125→    // Called during server shutdown. Clean up resources.
   126→  },
   127→
   128→  async install(ctx: InstallContext): Promise<void> {
   129→    // Called on `openacp plugin add`. Gather configuration interactively.
   130→  },
   131→
   132→  async configure(ctx: InstallContext): Promise<void> {
   133→    // Called on `openacp plugin configure`. Update settings.
   134→  },
   135→
   136→  async migrate(ctx: MigrateContext, oldSettings: unknown, oldVersion: string): Promise<unknown> {
   137→    // Called on boot when version changes. Migrate settings.
   138→    return oldSettings
   139→  },
   140→
   141→  async uninstall(ctx: InstallContext, opts: { purge: boolean }): Promise<void> {
   142→    // Called on `openacp plugin remove`. Clean up external resources.
   143→  },
   144→}
   145→
   146→export default plugin
   147→```
   148→
   149→**Lifecycle hooks summary:**
   150→
   151→| Hook | When it runs | Purpose |
   152→|---|---|---|
   153→| `setup(ctx)` | Server startup (dependency order) | Register services, commands, middleware, event listeners |
   154→| `teardown()` | Server shutdown (reverse order) | Clean up timers, connections, resources |
   155→| `install(ctx)` | `openacp plugin add` | Interactive first-time configuration |
   156→| `configure(ctx)` | `openacp plugin configure` | Re-configure settings |
   157→| `migrate(ctx, old, ver)` | Boot, when version changed | Migrate settings between versions |
   158→| `uninstall(ctx, opts)` | `openacp plugin remove` | Clean up external resources |
   159→
   160→---
   161→
   162→## Step 3: Development Workflow
   163→
   164→Install dependencies and build:
   165→
   166→```bash
   167→cd hello-world
   168→npm install
   169→npm run build
   170→```
   171→
   172→### Hot-reload development
   173→
   174→Start OpenACP in dev mode, pointing to your plugin directory:
   175→
   176→```bash
   177→openacp dev .
   178→```
   179→
   180→This will:
   181→1. Compile your TypeScript
   182→2. Start `tsc --watch` in the background
   183→3. Boot OpenACP with your plugin loaded
   184→4. Reload your plugin automatically when files change
   185→
   186→See [Dev Mode](dev-mode.md) for the full guide.
   187→
   188→### Run tests
   189→
   190→```bash
   191→npm test
   192→```
   193→
   194→Tests use Vitest and the `@openacp/plugin-sdk/testing` utilities.
   195→
   196→---
   197→
   198→## Step 4: Implement Your Plugin
   199→
   200→Let's turn the template into a greeting plugin that responds to a `/hello` command and logs session events.
   201→
   202→Replace the contents of `src/index.ts`:
   203→
   204→```typescript
   205→import type { OpenACPPlugin, PluginContext, InstallContext } from '@openacp/plugin-sdk'
   206→
   207→const plugin: OpenACPPlugin = {
   208→  name: '@myorg/hello-world',
   209→  version: '0.1.0',
   210→  description: 'A greeting plugin for OpenACP',
   211→
   212→  permissions: ['events:read', 'commands:register'],
   213→
   214→  async setup(ctx: PluginContext): Promise<void> {
   215→    // Register a /hello command
   216→    ctx.registerCommand({
   217→      name: 'hello',
   218→      description: 'Send a greeting',
   219→      usage: '[name]',
   220→      category: 'plugin',
   221→
   222→      async handler(args) {
   223→        const name = args.raw.trim() || 'World'
   224→        return { type: 'text', text: `Hello, ${name}! 👋` }
   225→      },
   226→    })
   227→
   228→    // Listen to session events
   229→    ctx.on('session:created', (event) => {
   230→      ctx.log.info(`New session started: ${event.sessionId}`)
   231→    })
   232→
   233→    ctx.on('session:afterDestroy', (event) => {
   234→      ctx.log.info(`Session ended: ${event.sessionId} (${event.durationMs}ms)`)
   235→    })
   236→
   237→    ctx.log.info('Hello World plugin ready')
   238→  },
   239→
   240→  async teardown(): Promise<void> {
   241→    // Nothing to clean up
   242→  },
   243→
   244→  async install(ctx: InstallContext): Promise<void> {
   245→    ctx.terminal.log.success('Hello World plugin installed!')
   246→  },
   247→}
   248→
   249→export default plugin
   250→```
   251→
   252→Build and test:
   253→
   254→```bash
   255→npm run build
   256→openacp dev .
   257→```
   258→
   259→Now in your messaging platform, type `/hello` or `/hello Alice` to see the plugin respond.
   260→
   261→---
   262→
   263→## Step 5: Test Your Plugin
   264→
   265→The scaffold includes a basic test. Let's expand it using the SDK testing utilities.
   266→
   267→Replace `src/__tests__/index.test.ts`:
   268→
   269→```typescript
   270→import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'
   271→import { createTestContext, createTestInstallContext } from '@openacp/plugin-sdk/testing'
   272→import plugin from '../index.js'
   273→
   274→describe('@myorg/hello-world', () => {
   275→  it('has correct metadata', () => {
   276→    expect(plugin.name).toBe('@myorg/hello-world')
   277→    expect(plugin.version).toBe('0.1.0')
   278→    expect(plugin.permissions).toContain('commands:register')
   279→  })
   280→
   281→  it('registers the /hello command on setup', async () => {
   282→    const ctx = createTestContext({ pluginName: '@myorg/hello-world' })
   283→    await plugin.setup(ctx)
   284→
   285→    expect(ctx.registeredCommands.has('hello')).toBe(true)
   286→    expect(ctx.registeredCommands.get('hello')!.description).toBe('Send a greeting')
   287→  })
   288→
   289→  it('/hello with no args returns default greeting', async () => {
   290→    const ctx = createTestContext({ pluginName: '@myorg/hello-world' })
   291→    await plugin.setup(ctx)
   292→
   293→    const response = await ctx.executeCommand('hello', { raw: '' })
   294→    expect(response).toEqual({ type: 'text', text: 'Hello, World! 👋' })
   295→  })
   296→
   297→  it('/hello with a name returns personalized greeting', async () => {
   298→    const ctx = createTestContext({ pluginName: '@myorg/hello-world' })
   299→    await plugin.setup(ctx)
   300→
   301→    const response = await ctx.executeCommand('hello', { raw: 'Alice' })
   302→    expect(response).toEqual({ type: 'text', text: 'Hello, Alice! 👋' })
   303→  })
   304→
   305→  it('emits log on session events', async () => {
   306→    const ctx = createTestContext({ pluginName: '@myorg/hello-world' })
   307→    await plugin.setup(ctx)
   308→
   309→    // Simulate a session:created event
   310→    ctx.emit('session:created', { sessionId: 'test-123' })
   311→    // No error thrown = event handler works
   312→  })
   313→
   314→  it('installs without errors', async () => {
   315→    const ctx = createTestInstallContext({
   316→      pluginName: '@myorg/hello-world',
   317→    })
   318→    await plugin.install!(ctx)
   319→
   320→    // Verify the install function ran
   321→    expect(ctx.terminalCalls).toHaveLength(0) // no prompts needed
   322→  })
   323→
   324→  it('tears down without errors', async () => {
   325→    await expect(plugin.teardown!()).resolves.not.toThrow()
   326→  })
   327→})
   328→```
   329→
   330→Run:
   331→
   332→```bash
   333→npm test
   334→```
   335→
   336→See [Plugin SDK Reference](plugin-sdk-reference.md) for the full testing API including `createTestContext`, `createTestInstallContext`, and `mockServices`.
   337→
   338→---
   339→
   340→## Step 6: Configure and Install
   341→
   342→### Install your plugin locally
   343→
   344→For testing with a real OpenACP instance (not dev mode):
   345→
   346→```bash
   347→# From the plugin directory, build first
   348→npm run build
   349→
   350→# Install from local path
   351→openacp plugin add ./hello-world
   352→```
   353→
   354→### Plugin settings
   355→
   356→If your plugin needs configuration (API keys, preferences), define a `settingsSchema` with Zod and use the `install()` hook:
   357→
   358→```typescript
   359→import { z } from 'zod'
   360→
   361→const settingsSchema = z.object({
   362→  defaultName: z.string().default('World'),
   363→})
   364→
   365→const plugin: OpenACPPlugin = {
   366→  // ...
   367→  settingsSchema,
   368→
   369→  async install(ctx: InstallContext) {
   370→    const name = await ctx.terminal.text({
   371→      message: 'Default greeting name:',
   372→      placeholder: 'World',
   373→    })
   374→    await ctx.settings.set('defaultName', name || 'World')
   375→    ctx.terminal.log.success('Configured!')
   376→  },
   377→
   378→  async setup(ctx: PluginContext) {
   379→    const defaultName = ctx.pluginConfig.defaultName ?? 'World'
   380→    // Use defaultName in your command handler...
   381→  },
   382→}
   383→```
   384→
   385→### Enable / disable
   386→
   387→```bash
   388→openacp plugin enable @myorg/hello-world
   389→openacp plugin disable @myorg/hello-world
   390→```
   391→
   392→### Reconfigure
   393→
   394→```bash
   395→openacp plugin configure @myorg/hello-world
   396→```
   397→
   398→---
   399→
   400→## Step 7: Publish
   401→
   402→### Prepare for publishing
   403→
   404→1. Update `version` in both `package.json` and `src/index.ts`
   405→2. Make sure `main` points to `dist/index.js`
   406→3. Ensure `keywords` includes `openacp` and `openacp-plugin`
   407→
   408→### Build and publish
   409→
   410→```bash
   411→npm run build
   412→npm test
   413→npm publish --access public
   414→```
   415→
   416→### How users install your plugin
   417→
   418→```bash
   419→openacp plugin add @myorg/hello-world
   420→```
   421→
   422→This downloads from npm into `~/.openacp/plugins/`, validates the plugin interface, and runs `install()` if defined.
   423→
   424→---
   425→

   427→

   429→- [Plugin SDK Reference](plugin-sdk-reference.md) -- complete API reference for types, base classes, and testing utilities

content.text:
I now have all the information needed for a thorough review. Here is the full assessment.

---

**Status: ISSUES_FOUND**

---

## Issues

**Issue 1 — Critical: npm scope inconsistency (`@open-acp` vs `@openacp`)**

The spec names the new package `@open-acp/plugin-discord` (with a hyphen in the scope), but every other package in this project uses the `@openacp` scope: `@openacp/cli`, `@openacp/plugin-sdk`. The microkernel architecture proposal document (`docs/proposal/microkernel-lifecycle-architecture.md`) also lists the planned package name as `@openacp/plugin-discord`.

More critically, the legacy config migration map hardcoded in `src/core/plugin/lifecycle-manager.ts` line 40 uses `'@openacp/discord'` as the key for the Discord config section:

```typescript
'@openacp/discord': 'channels.discord',
```

The current plugin's `name` field in `src/plugins/discord/index.ts` line 9 is also `'@openacp/discord'`. If the extracted package is published as `@open-acp/plugin-discord`, this legacy migration mapping will never match, silently breaking config migration for existing users on upgrade. This is a backward compatibility violation per the project's own CLAUDE.md standards.

**Fix:** Change the spec to use `@openacp/plugin-discord` consistently, and update the legacy migration map key when the plugin is renamed.

---

**Issue 2 — Critical: `runAdapterConformanceTests` does not exist in the SDK**

The Testing section states:

> Conformance test: Import `runAdapterConformanceTests` from `@openacp/plugin-sdk/testing`

The actual SDK testing module at `/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/OpenACP/packages/plugin-sdk/src/testing.ts` exports only:

```typescript
export { createTestContext } from './testing/test-context.js'
export { createTestInstallContext } from './testing/test-install-context.js'
export { mockServices } from './testing/mock-services.js'
```

There is no `runAdapterConformanceTests` anywhere in the SDK. A developer following this spec would write an import that fails at compile time. The spec either needs to describe adding this utility to the SDK as part of the work, or the testing section needs to be corrected to reflect the actual available utilities.

# Extract Discord Plugin to Standalone Package

## Problem

The Discord adapter is bundled as a built-in plugin in OpenACP, meaning `discord.js` and its dependencies are installed for all users even if they don't use Discord. This adds unnecessary weight. The plugin should be a separate package that users install only when needed.

## Solution

Extract `src/plugins/discord/` from the OpenACP monorepo into a standalone package `@open-acp/plugin-discord` in a separate repository. Extend `@openacp/plugin-sdk` to export all types/classes the Discord plugin needs. Remove the Discord plugin from the OpenACP repo.

## Target Repository

`/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/discord-plugin/` → published as `@open-acp/plugin-discord` on npm.

## Standalone Plugin Structure

```
discord-plugin/
  src/
    index.ts                    # Plugin entry (OpenACPPlugin interface)
    adapter.ts                  # DiscordAdapter (extends MessagingAdapter)
    renderer.ts                 # Discord-specific message rendering
    formatting.ts               # Markdown formatting for Discord
    streaming.ts                # Message streaming/chunking
    draft-manager.ts            # Draft message management
    tool-call-tracker.ts        # Tool call display
    skill-command-manager.ts    # Skill command UI
    activity.ts                 # Activity indicators
    permissions.ts              # Permission request buttons
    forums.ts                   # Forum channel management
    assistant.ts                # Assistant topic handler
    action-detect.ts            # Action detection
    media.ts                    # Media/file handling
    types.ts                    # Discord-specific types
    validators.ts               # Config validation
    commands/
      index.ts
      admin.ts
      agents.ts
      doctor.ts
      integrate.ts
      menu.ts
      new-session.ts
      router.ts
      session.ts
      settings.ts
    __tests__/
      conformance.test.ts
      formatting.test.ts
      media.test.ts
  package.json
  tsconfig.json
  .gitignore
  README.md
```

### `package.json`

```json
{
  "name": "@open-acp/plugin-discord",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "type": "module",
  "main": "dist/index.js",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "tsc",
    "dev": "tsc --watch",
    "test": "vitest",
    "prepublishOnly": "npm run build"
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "@openacp/plugin-sdk": "^1.0.0"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "discord.js": "^14.x"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@openacp/plugin-sdk": "^1.0.0",
    "typescript": "^5.4.0",
    "vitest": "^3.0.0"
  }
}
```

## Import Migration

All `../../core/` imports in the Discord plugin will be replaced with imports from `@openacp/plugin-sdk`.

### Already exported by Plugin SDK (no SDK changes needed)

- Plugin interfaces: `OpenACPPlugin`, `PluginContext`, `InstallContext`, `CommandDef`, `CommandResponse`, `MenuOption`, `ListItem`
- Service interfaces: `SecurityService`, `FileServiceInterface`, `NotificationService`, `UsageService`, `SpeechServiceInterface`, `TunnelServiceInterface`, `ContextService`
- Adapter types: `IChannelAdapter`, `OutgoingMessage`, `PermissionRequest`, `NotificationMessage`, `AgentCommand`, `AdapterCapabilities`
- Adapter base classes: `MessagingAdapter`, `StreamAdapter`, `BaseRenderer`
- Adapter primitives: `SendQueue`, `DraftManager`, `ToolCallTracker`, `ActivityTracker`

### Need to add to Plugin SDK

These are currently internal to `@openacp/cli` and need to be re-exported from `@openacp/plugin-sdk`:

**Core classes:**
- `OpenACPCore` — needed by adapter to access core methods
- `Session` — needed for session interaction
- `SessionManager` — needed for session lookup
- `CommandRegistry` — needed for command routing

**Doctor system:**
- `DoctorEngine`, `DoctorReport`, `PendingFix` — needed for `/doctor` command

**Config utilities:**
- `ConfigFieldDef`, `getSafeFields`, `resolveOptions`, `getConfigValue`, `isHotReloadable` — needed for `/settings` command

**Data:**
- `PRODUCT_GUIDE` — product guide text used in assistant topic

**Format types:**
- `DisplayVerbosity`, `ToolCallMeta`, `ToolUpdateMeta`, `ViewerLinks`, `STATUS_ICONS`, `KIND_ICONS`

**Format utilities:**
- `progressBar`, `formatTokens`, `truncateContent`, `stripCodeFences`, `splitMessage`

**Message formatter:**
- `extractContentText`, `formatToolSummary`, `formatToolTitle`, `resolveToolIcon`

**Types:**
- `SessionStatus`, `ConfigOption`, `UsageRecord`, `UsageSummary`, `PlanEntry`, `Attachment`, `StopReason`, `DiscordPlatformData`, `InstallProgress`

**Rendering:**
- `IRenderer`, `RenderedMessage`

## Changes to OpenACP Repo

### Remove from OpenACP

1. Delete `src/plugins/discord/` entirely
2. Remove Discord registration from `src/plugins/core-plugins.ts`
3. Remove `discord.js` from `package.json` dependencies

### Extend Plugin SDK

Add all missing re-exports listed above to `packages/plugin-sdk/src/index.ts`. All re-exports come from `@openacp/cli` — the SDK is a thin re-export layer, no new code.

### No changes needed

- Core plugin loader works as-is for external plugins
- Config schema, session management, adapter interface unchanged
- `openacp plugin add` command handles npm install of plugin + its dependencies

## User Installation Flow

```bash
# Install from npm (after publishing)
openacp plugin add @open-acp/plugin-discord

# Install from local path (development)
openacp plugin add /path/to/discord-plugin

# Development with hot-reload
openacp dev /path/to/discord-plugin

# Uninstall
openacp plugin remove @open-acp/plugin-discord
```

When installed, `discord.js` is npm-installed as a dependency of the plugin. When not installed, OpenACP has zero Discord-related dependencies.

## Testing

### Standalone repo tests

- **Conformance test**: Import `runAdapterConformanceTests` from `@openacp/plugin-sdk/testing`
- **Unit tests**: Copy existing formatting.test.ts, media.test.ts from OpenACP
- **Dev mode**: `openacp dev .` in the plugin directory for hot-reload testing

### Edge cases

- Plugin installed but Discord bot token not configured: plugin's `install()` should prompt for token
- Plugin removed while Discord sessions active: graceful shutdown of Discord adapter
- SDK version mismatch: peerDependency warning from npm

## Files Modified (Summary)

### OpenACP repo
- `packages/plugin-sdk/src/index.ts` — Add ~30 re-exports
- `src/plugins/core-plugins.ts` — Remove Discord registration
- `src/plugins/discord/` — Delete entirely
- `package.json` — Remove `discord.js` dependency

### New discord-plugin repo
- All 29 files from `src/plugins/discord/` copied and refactored
- New `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `.gitignore`, `README.md`
- All `../../core/` imports replaced with `@openacp/plugin-sdk`

- `DisplayVerbosity`, `ToolCallMeta`, `ToolUpdateMeta`, `ViewerLinks`, `STATUS_ICONS`, `KIND_ICONS`

**Format utilities:**
- `progressBar`, `formatTokens`, `truncateContent`, `stripCodeFences`, `splitMessage`

**Message formatter:**
- `extractContentText`, `formatToolSummary`, `formatToolTitle`, `resolveToolIcon`

**Core classes:**
- `OpenACPCore` — needed by adapter to access core methods
- `Session` — needed for session interaction
- `SessionManager` — needed for session lookup
- `CommandRegistry` — needed for command routing
- `AgentCatalog` — accessed via `core.agentCatalog`

**Doctor system:**
- `DoctorEngine`, `DoctorReport`, `PendingFix` — needed for `/doctor` command

**Config utilities:**
- `ConfigFieldDef`, `getSafeFields`, `resolveOptions`, `getConfigValue`, `isHotReloadable` — needed for `/settings` command

- `requestRestart` — accessed by admin commands

- SDK version mismatch: peerDependency warning from npm

- `src/core/plugin/lifecycle-manager.ts` — Add `@openacp/plugin-discord` to migration map
- `src/plugins/core-plugins.ts` — Remove Discord registration
- `src/plugins/discord/` — Delete entirely

# Extract Discord Plugin to Standalone Package

## Problem

The Discord adapter is bundled as a built-in plugin in OpenACP, meaning `discord.js` and its dependencies are installed for all users even if they don't use Discord. This adds unnecessary weight. The plugin should be a separate package that users install only when needed.

## Solution

Extract `src/plugins/discord/` from the OpenACP monorepo into a standalone package `@open-acp/plugin-discord` in a separate repository. Extend `@openacp/plugin-sdk` to export all types/classes the Discord plugin needs. Remove the Discord plugin from the OpenACP repo.

## Target Repository

`/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/discord-plugin/` → published as `@open-acp/plugin-discord` on npm.

## Standalone Plugin Structure

```
discord-plugin/
  src/
    index.ts                    # Plugin entry (OpenACPPlugin interface)
    adapter.ts                  # DiscordAdapter (extends MessagingAdapter)
    renderer.ts                 # Discord-specific message rendering
    formatting.ts               # Markdown formatting for Discord
    streaming.ts                # Message streaming/chunking
    draft-manager.ts            # Draft message management
    tool-call-tracker.ts        # Tool call display
    skill-command-manager.ts    # Skill command UI
    activity.ts                 # Activity indicators
    permissions.ts              # Permission request buttons
    forums.ts                   # Forum channel management
    assistant.ts                # Assistant topic handler
    action-detect.ts            # Action detection
    media.ts                    # Media/file handling
    types.ts                    # Discord-specific types
    validators.ts               # Config validation
    commands/
      index.ts
      admin.ts
      agents.ts
      doctor.ts
      integrate.ts
      menu.ts
      new-session.ts
      router.ts
      session.ts
      settings.ts
    __tests__/
      conformance.test.ts
      formatting.test.ts
      media.test.ts
  package.json
  tsconfig.json
  .gitignore
  README.md
```

### `package.json`

```json
{
  "name": "@open-acp/plugin-discord",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "type": "module",
  "main": "dist/index.js",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "tsc",
    "dev": "tsc --watch",
    "test": "vitest",
    "prepublishOnly": "npm run build"
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "@openacp/plugin-sdk": "^1.0.0"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "discord.js": "^14.x"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@openacp/plugin-sdk": "^1.0.0",
    "typescript": "^5.4.0",
    "vitest": "^3.0.0"
  }
}
```

## Import Migration

All `../../core/` imports in the Discord plugin will be replaced with imports from `@openacp/plugin-sdk`.

### Already exported by Plugin SDK (no SDK changes needed)

- Plugin interfaces: `OpenACPPlugin`, `PluginContext`, `InstallContext`, `CommandDef`, `CommandResponse`, `MenuOption`, `ListItem`
- Service interfaces: `SecurityService`, `FileServiceInterface`, `NotificationService`, `UsageService`, `SpeechServiceInterface`, `TunnelServiceInterface`, `ContextService`
- Adapter types: `IChannelAdapter`, `OutgoingMessage`, `PermissionRequest`, `NotificationMessage`, `AgentCommand`, `AdapterCapabilities`
- Adapter base classes: `MessagingAdapter`, `StreamAdapter`, `BaseRenderer`
- Adapter primitives: `SendQueue`, `DraftManager`, `ToolCallTracker`, `ActivityTracker`

### Need to add to Plugin SDK

These are currently internal to `@openacp/cli` and need to be re-exported from `@openacp/plugin-sdk`:

**Core classes:**
- `OpenACPCore` — needed by adapter to access core methods
- `Session` — needed for session interaction
- `SessionManager` — needed for session lookup
- `CommandRegistry` — needed for command routing

**Doctor system:**
- `DoctorEngine`, `DoctorReport`, `PendingFix` — needed for `/doctor` command

**Config utilities:**
- `ConfigFieldDef`, `getSafeFields`, `resolveOptions`, `getConfigValue`, `isHotReloadable` — needed for `/settings` command

**Data:**
- `PRODUCT_GUIDE` — product guide text used in assistant topic

**Format types:**
- `DisplayVerbosity`, `ToolCallMeta`, `ToolUpdateMeta`, `ViewerLinks`, `STATUS_ICONS`, `KIND_ICONS`

**Format utilities:**
- `progressBar`, `formatTokens`, `truncateContent`, `stripCodeFences`, `splitMessage`

**Message formatter:**
- `extractContentText`, `formatToolSummary`, `formatToolTitle`, `resolveToolIcon`

**Types:**
- `SessionStatus`, `ConfigOption`, `UsageRecord`, `UsageSummary`, `PlanEntry`, `Attachment`, `StopReason`, `DiscordPlatformData`, `InstallProgress`

**Rendering:**
- `IRenderer`, `RenderedMessage`

## Changes to OpenACP Repo

### Remove from OpenACP

1. Delete `src/plugins/discord/` entirely
2. Remove Discord registration from `src/plugins/core-plugins.ts`
3. Remove `discord.js` from `package.json` dependencies

### Extend Plugin SDK

Add all missing re-exports listed above to `packages/plugin-sdk/src/index.ts`. All re-exports come from `@openacp/cli` — the SDK is a thin re-export layer, no new code.

### No changes needed

- Core plugin loader works as-is for external plugins
- Config schema, session management, adapter interface unchanged
- `openacp plugin add` command handles npm install of plugin + its dependencies

## User Installation Flow

```bash
# Install from npm (after publishing)
openacp plugin add @open-acp/plugin-discord

# Install from local path (development)
openacp plugin add /path/to/discord-plugin

# Development with hot-reload
openacp dev /path/to/discord-plugin

# Uninstall
openacp plugin remove @open-acp/plugin-discord
```

When installed, `discord.js` is npm-installed as a dependency of the plugin. When not installed, OpenACP has zero Discord-related dependencies.

## Testing

### Standalone repo tests

- **Conformance test**: Import `runAdapterConformanceTests` from `@openacp/plugin-sdk/testing`
- **Unit tests**: Copy existing formatting.test.ts, media.test.ts from OpenACP
- **Dev mode**: `openacp dev .` in the plugin directory for hot-reload testing

### Edge cases

- Plugin installed but Discord bot token not configured: plugin's `install()` should prompt for token
- Plugin removed while Discord sessions active: graceful shutdown of Discord adapter
- SDK version mismatch: peerDependency warning from npm

## Files Modified (Summary)

### OpenACP repo
- `packages/plugin-sdk/src/index.ts` — Add ~30 re-exports
- `src/plugins/core-plugins.ts` — Remove Discord registration
- `src/plugins/discord/` — Delete entirely
- `package.json` — Remove `discord.js` dependency

### New discord-plugin repo
- All 29 files from `src/plugins/discord/` copied and refactored
- New `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `.gitignore`, `README.md`
- All `../../core/` imports replaced with `@openacp/plugin-sdk`

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** This should be run in a dedicated worktree (created by brainstorming skill).

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py

1→import type { OpenACPPlugin, InstallContext } from '../../core/plugin/types.js'
     2→import type { OpenACPCore } from '../../core/core.js'
     3→import type { DiscordChannelConfig } from './types.js'
     4→
     5→function createDiscordPlugin(): OpenACPPlugin {
     6→  let adapter: { stop(): Promise<void> } | null = null
     7→
     8→  return {
     9→    name: '@openacp/discord',
    10→    version: '1.0.0',
    11→    description: 'Discord adapter with forum threads',
    12→    essential: true,
    13→    pluginDependencies: {
    14→      '@openacp/security': '^1.0.0',
    15→      '@openacp/notifications': '^1.0.0',
    16→    },
    17→    optionalPluginDependencies: {
    18→      '@openacp/speech': '^1.0.0',
    19→    },
    20→    permissions: ['services:register', 'kernel:access', 'events:read'],
    21→
    22→    async install(ctx: InstallContext) {
    23→      const { terminal, settings, legacyConfig } = ctx
    24→
    25→      // Migrate from legacy config if present
    26→      if (legacyConfig) {
    27→        const ch = legacyConfig.channels as Record<string, unknown> | undefined
    28→        const discordCfg = ch?.discord as Record<string, unknown> | undefined
    29→        if (discordCfg?.botToken) {
    30→          await settings.setAll({
    31→            botToken: discordCfg.botToken,
    32→            guildId: discordCfg.guildId,
    33→            forumChannelId: discordCfg.forumChannelId ?? null,
    34→            notificationChannelId: discordCfg.notificationChannelId ?? null,
    35→            assistantThreadId: discordCfg.assistantThreadId ?? null,
    36→          })
    37→          terminal.log.success('Discord settings migrated from legacy config')
    38→          return
    39→        }
    40→      }
    41→
    42→      // Interactive setup via terminal
    43→      const { validateDiscordToken } = await import('./validators.js')
    44→
    45→      terminal.note(
    46→        '1. Create app at https://discord.com/developers/applications\n' +
    47→        '2. Go to Bot > Reset Token > copy it\n' +
    48→        '3. Enable Message Content Intent (Bot > Privileged Intents)\n' +
    49→        '4. OAuth2 > URL Generator > scopes: bot + applications.commands\n' +
    50→        '5. Bot Permissions: Manage Channels, Send Messages, Manage Threads, Attach Files\n' +
    51→        '6. Open generated URL > invite bot to your server',
    52→        'Discord Setup',
    53→      )
    54→
    55→      let botToken = ''
    56→      while (true) {
    57→        botToken = await terminal.text({
    58→          message: 'Bot token (from Discord Developer Portal):',
    59→          validate: (val) => {
    60→            if (!val.trim()) return 'Token cannot be empty'
    61→            return undefined
    62→          },
    63→        })
    64→        botToken = botToken.trim()
    65→
    66→        const spin = terminal.spinner()
    67→        spin.start('Validating token...')
    68→        const result = await validateDiscordToken(botToken)
    69→        if (result.ok) {
    70→          spin.stop(`Connected as @${result.username} (id: ${result.id})`)
    71→          break
    72→        }
    73→        spin.fail(result.error)
    74→        const action = await terminal.select({
    75→          message: 'What to do?',
    76→          options: [
    77→            { label: 'Re-enter token', value: 'retry' },
    78→            { label: 'Use as-is (skip validation)', value: 'skip' },
    79→          ],
    80→        })
    81→        if (action === 'skip') break
    82→      }
    83→
    84→      const guildId = await terminal.text({
    85→        message: 'Guild (server) ID:',
    86→        validate: (val) => {
    87→          const trimmed = val.trim()
    88→          if (!trimmed) return 'Guild ID cannot be empty'
    89→          if (!/^\d{17,20}$/.test(trimmed)) return 'Guild ID must be a numeric Discord snowflake (17-20 digits)'
    90→          return undefined
    91→        },
    92→      })
    93→
    94→      await settings.setAll({
    95→        botToken,
    96→        guildId: guildId.trim(),
    97→        forumChannelId: null,
    98→        notificationChannelId: null,
    99→        assistantThreadId: null,
   100→      })
   101→      terminal.log.success('Discord settings saved')
   102→    },
   103→
   104→    async configure(ctx: InstallContext) {
   105→      const { terminal, settings } = ctx
   106→      const current = await settings.getAll()
   107→
   108→      const choice = await terminal.select({
   109→        message: 'What to configure?',
   110→        options: [
   111→          { value: 'token', label: 'Change bot token' },
   112→          { value: 'guildId', label: 'Change guild ID' },
   113→          { value: 'done', label: 'Done' },
   114→        ],
   115→      })
   116→
   117→      if (choice === 'token') {
   118→        const token = await terminal.text({
   119→          message: 'New bot token:',
   120→          validate: (v) => (!v.trim() ? 'Token cannot be empty' : undefined),
   121→        })
   122→        await settings.set('botToken', token.trim())
   123→        terminal.log.success('Bot token updated')
   124→      } else if (choice === 'guildId') {
   125→        const val = await terminal.text({
   126→          message: 'New guild ID:',
   127→          defaultValue: (current.guildId as string) ?? '',
   128→          validate: (v) => {
   129→            const trimmed = v.trim()
   130→            if (!trimmed) return 'Guild ID cannot be empty'
   131→            if (!/^\d{17,20}$/.test(trimmed)) return 'Guild ID must be a numeric Discord snowflake (17-20 digits)'
   132→            return undefined
   133→          },
   134→        })
   135→        await settings.set('guildId', val.trim())
   136→        terminal.log.success('Guild ID updated')
   137→      }
   138→    },
   139→
   140→    async uninstall(ctx: InstallContext, opts: { purge: boolean }) {
   141→      if (opts.purge) {
   142→        await ctx.settings.clear()
   143→        ctx.terminal.log.success('Discord settings cleared')
   144→      }
   145→    },
   146→
   147→    async setup(ctx) {
   148→      const config = ctx.pluginConfig as Record<string, unknown>
   149→      if (!config.botToken || !config.guildId) {
   150→        ctx.log.info('Discord disabled (missing botToken or guildId)')
   151→        return
   152→      }
   153→
   154→      const { DiscordAdapter } = await import('./adapter.js')
   155→      // config is a Record<string, unknown> from pluginConfig; at runtime it
   156→      // contains all DiscordChannelConfig fields populated from the migrated config.
   157→      adapter = new DiscordAdapter(ctx.core as OpenACPCore, {
   158→        ...config,
   159→        enabled: true,
   160→        maxMessageLength: 2000,
   161→      } as unknown as DiscordChannelConfig)
   162→
   163→      ctx.registerService('adapter:discord', adapter)
   164→      ctx.log.info('Discord adapter registered')
   165→    },
   166→
   167→    async teardown() {
   168→      if (adapter) {
   169→        await adapter.stop()
   170→      }
   171→    },
   172→  }
   173→}
   174→
   175→export default createDiscordPlugin()
   176→

1→/**
     2→ * OpenACP Product Guide — comprehensive reference for the AI assistant.
     3→ * The assistant reads this at runtime to answer user questions about features.
     4→ */
     5→export const PRODUCT_GUIDE = `
     6→# OpenACP — Product Guide
     7→
     8→OpenACP lets you chat with AI coding agents (like Claude Code) through messaging platforms (Telegram, Discord).
     9→You type messages in your chat platform, the agent reads/writes/runs code in your project folder, and results stream back in real time.
    10→
    11→---
    12→
    13→## Quick Start
    14→
    15→1. Start OpenACP: \`openacp\` (or \`openacp start\` for background daemon)
    16→2. Open your messaging platform (Telegram group or Discord server) — you'll see the Assistant topic/thread
    17→3. Tap/click 🆕 New Session or type /new
    18→4. Pick an agent and a project folder
    19→5. Chat in the session topic/thread — the agent works on your code
    20→
    21→---
    22→
    23→## Core Concepts
    24→
    25→### Sessions
    26→A session = one conversation with one AI agent working in one project folder.
    27→Each session gets its own topic (Telegram) or forum thread (Discord). Chat there to give instructions to the agent.
    28→
    29→### Agents
    30→An agent is an AI coding tool (e.g., Claude Code, Gemini, Cursor, Codex, etc.).
    31→OpenACP supports 28+ agents from the official ACP Registry (agentclientprotocol.com).
    32→You can install multiple agents and choose which one to use per session.
    33→The default agent is used when you don't specify one.
    34→
    35→### Agent Management
    36→- Browse agents: \`/agents\` in your chat platform or \`openacp agents\` in CLI
    37→- Install: tap the install button in /agents, or \`openacp agents install <name>\`
    38→- Uninstall: \`openacp agents uninstall <name>\`
    39→- Setup/login: \`openacp agents run <name> -- <args>\` (e.g., \`openacp agents run gemini -- auth login\`)
    40→- Details: \`openacp agents info <name>\` shows version, dependencies, and setup steps
    41→
    42→Some agents need additional setup before they can be used:
    43→- Claude: requires \`claude login\`
    44→- Gemini: requires \`openacp agents run gemini -- auth login\`
    45→- Codex: requires setting \`OPENAI_API_KEY\` environment variable
    46→- GitHub Copilot: requires \`openacp agents run copilot -- auth login\`
    47→
    48→Agents are installed in three ways depending on the agent:
    49→- **npx** — Node.js agents, downloaded automatically on first use
    50→- **uvx** — Python agents, downloaded automatically on first use
    51→- **binary** — Platform-specific binaries, downloaded to \`~/.openacp/agents/\`
    52→
    53→### Project Folder (Workspace)
    54→The directory where the agent reads, writes, and runs code.
    55→When creating a session, you choose which folder the agent works in.
    56→You can type a full path like \`~/code/my-project\` or just a name like \`my-project\` (it becomes \`<base-dir>/my-project\`).
    57→
    58→### System Topics
    59→- **Assistant** — Always-on helper that can answer questions, create sessions, check status, troubleshoot
    60→- **Notifications** — System alerts (permission requests, session errors, completions)
    61→
    62→---
    63→
    64→## Creating Sessions
    65→
    66→### From menu
    67→Tap 🆕 New Session → choose agent (if multiple) → choose project folder → confirm
    68→
    69→### From command
    70→- \`/new\` — Interactive flow (asks agent + folder)
    71→- \`/new claude ~/code/my-project\` — Create directly with specific agent and folder
    72→
    73→### From Assistant topic
    74→Just ask: "Create a session for my-project with claude" — the assistant handles it
    75→
    76→### Quick new chat
    77→\`/newchat\` in a session topic — creates new session with same agent and folder as current one
    78→
    79→---
    80→
    81→## Working with Sessions
    82→
    83→### Chat
    84→Type messages in the session topic. The agent responds with code changes, explanations, tool outputs.
    85→
    86→### What you see while the agent works
    87→- **💭 Thinking indicator** — Shows when the agent is reasoning, with elapsed time
    88→- **Text responses** — Streamed in real time, updated every few seconds
    89→- **Tool calls** — When the agent runs commands or edits files, you see tool name, input, status, and output
    90→- **📋 Plan card** — Visual task progress with completed/in-progress/pending items and progress bar
    91→- **"View File" / "View Diff" buttons** — Opens in browser with Monaco editor (requires tunnel)
    92→
    93→### Session lifecycle
    94→1. **Creating** — Topic created, agent spawning
    95→2. **Warming up** — Agent primes its cache (happens automatically, invisible to you)
    96→3. **Active** — Ready for your messages
    97→4. **Auto-naming** — After your first message, the session gets a descriptive name (agent summarizes in ~5 words). The topic title updates automatically.
    98→5. **Finished/Error** — Session completed or hit an error
    99→
   100→### Agent skills
   101→Some agents provide slash commands (e.g., /compact, /review). Available skills are pinned in the session topic.
   102→
   103→### Permission requests
   104→When the agent wants to run a command, it asks for permission.
   105→You see buttons: ✅ Allow, ❌ Reject (and sometimes "Always Allow").
   106→A notification also appears in the Notifications topic with a link to the request.
   107→
   108→### Dangerous mode
   109→Auto-approves ALL permission requests — the agent runs any command without asking.
   110→- Enable: \`/enable_dangerous\` or tap the ☠️ button in the session
   111→- Disable: \`/disable_dangerous\` or tap the 🔐 button
   112→- ⚠️ Use with caution — the agent can execute anything
   113→
   114→### Session timeout
   115→Idle sessions are automatically cancelled after a configurable timeout (default: 60 minutes).
   116→Configure via \`security.sessionTimeoutMinutes\` in config.
   117→
   118→---
   119→
   120→## Session Transfer (Handoff)
   121→
   122→### Chat → Terminal
   123→1. Type \`/handoff\` in a session topic/thread
   124→2. You get a command like \`claude --resume <SESSION_ID>\`
   125→3. Copy and run it in your terminal — the session continues there with full conversation history
   126→
   127→### Terminal → Chat
   128→1. First time: run \`openacp integrate claude\` to install the handoff skill (one-time setup)
   129→2. In Claude Code, use the /openacp:handoff slash command
   130→3. The session appears as a new topic/thread and you can continue chatting there
   131→
   132→### How it works
   133→- The agent session ID is shared between platforms
   134→- Conversation history is preserved — pick up where you left off
   135→- The agent that supports resume (e.g., Claude with \`--resume\`) handles the actual transfer
   136→
   137→---
   138→
   139→## Managing Sessions
   140→
   141→### Status
   142→- \`/status\` — Shows active sessions count and details
   143→- Ask the Assistant: "What sessions are running?"
   144→
   145→### List all sessions
   146→- \`/sessions\` — Shows all sessions with status (active, finished, error)
   147→
   148→### Cancel
   149→- \`/cancel\` in a session topic — cancels that session
   150→- Ask the Assistant: "Cancel the stuck session"
   151→
   152→### Cleanup
   153→- From \`/sessions\` → tap cleanup buttons (finished, errors, all)
   154→- Ask the Assistant: "Clean up old sessions"
   155→
   156→---
   157→
   158→## Assistant Topic
   159→
   160→The Assistant is an always-on AI helper in its own topic. It can:
   161→- Answer questions about OpenACP
   162→- Create sessions for you
   163→- Check status and health
   164→- Cancel sessions
   165→- Clean up old sessions
   166→- Troubleshoot issues
   167→- Manage configuration
   168→
   169→Just chat naturally: "How do I create a session?", "What's the status?", "Something is stuck"
   170→
   171→### Clear history
   172→\`/clear\` in the Assistant topic — resets the conversation
   173→
   174→---
   175→
   176→## System Commands
   177→
   178→| Command | Where | What it does |
   179→|---------|-------|-------------|
   180→| \`/new [agent] [path]\` | Anywhere | Create new session |
   181→| \`/newchat\` | Session topic | New session, same agent + folder |
   182→| \`/cancel\` | Session topic | Cancel current session |
   183→| \`/status\` | Anywhere | Show status |
   184→| \`/sessions\` | Anywhere | List all sessions |
   185→| \`/agents\` | Anywhere | Browse & install agents from ACP Registry |
   186→| \`/install <name>\` | Anywhere | Install an agent |
   187→| \`/enable_dangerous\` | Session topic | Auto-approve all permissions |
   188→| \`/disable_dangerous\` | Session topic | Restore permission prompts |
   189→| \`/handoff\` | Session topic | Transfer session to terminal |
   190→| \`/clear\` | Assistant topic | Clear assistant history |
   191→| \`/menu\` | Anywhere | Show action menu |
   192→| \`/help\` | Anywhere | Show help |
   193→| \`/restart\` | Anywhere | Restart OpenACP |
   194→| \`/update\` | Anywhere | Update to latest version |
   195→| \`/integrate\` | Anywhere | Manage agent integrations |
   196→
   197→---
   198→
   199→## Menu Buttons
   200→
   201→| Button | Action |
   202→|--------|--------|
   203→| 🆕 New Session | Create new session (interactive) |
   204→| 📋 Sessions | List all sessions with cleanup options |
   205→| 📊 Status | Show active/total session count |
   206→| 🤖 Agents | List available agents |
   207→| 🔗 Integrate | Manage agent integrations |
   208→| ❓ Help | Show help text |
   209→| 🔄 Restart | Restart OpenACP |
   210→| ⬆️ Update | Check and install updates |
   211→
   212→---
   213→
   214→## CLI Commands
   215→
   216→### Server
   217→- \`openacp\` — Start (uses configured mode: foreground or daemon)
   218→- \`openacp start\` — Start as background daemon
   219→- \`openacp stop\` — Stop daemon
   220→- \`openacp status\` — Show daemon status
   221→- \`openacp logs\` — Tail daemon logs
   222→- \`openacp --foreground\` — Force foreground mode (useful for debugging or containers)
   223→
   224→### Auto-start (run on boot)
   225→- macOS: installs a LaunchAgent in \`~/Library/LaunchAgents/\`
   226→- Linux: installs a systemd user service in \`~/.config/systemd/user/\`
   227→- Enabled automatically when you start the daemon. Remove with \`openacp stop\`.
   228→
   229→### Configuration
   230→- \`openacp config\` — Interactive config editor
   231→- \`openacp reset\` — Delete all data and start fresh
   232→
   233→### Agent Management (CLI)
   234→- \`openacp agents\` — List all agents (installed + available from ACP Registry)
   235→- \`openacp agents install <name>\` — Install an agent
   236→- \`openacp agents uninstall <name>\` — Remove an agent
   237→- \`openacp agents info <name>\` — Show details, dependencies, and setup guide
   238→- \`openacp agents run <name> [-- args]\` — Run agent CLI directly (for login, config, etc.)
   239→- \`openacp agents refresh\` — Force-refresh registry cache
   240→
   241→### Plugins
   242→- \`openacp install <package>\` — Install adapter plugin
   243→- \`openacp uninstall <package>\` — Remove adapter plugin
   244→- \`openacp plugins\` — List installed plugins
   245→
   246→### Integration
   247→- \`openacp integrate <agent>\` — Install agent integration (e.g., Claude handoff skill)
   248→- \`openacp integrate <agent> --uninstall\` — Remove integration
   249→
   250→### API (requires running daemon)
   251→\`openacp api <command>\` — Interact with running daemon:
   252→
   253→| Command | Description |
   254→|---------|-------------|
   255→| \`status\` | List active sessions |
   256→| \`session <id>\` | Session details |
   257→| \`new <agent> <path>\` | Create session |
   258→| \`send <id> "text"\` | Send prompt |
   259→| \`cancel <id>\` | Cancel session |
   260→| \`dangerous <id> on/off\` | Toggle dangerous mode |
   261→| \`topics [--status x,y]\` | List topics |
   262→| \`delete-topic <id> [--force]\` | Delete topic |
   263→| \`cleanup [--status x,y]\` | Cleanup old topics |
   264→| \`agents\` | List agents |
   265→| \`health\` | System health |
   266→| \`config\` | Show config |
   267→| \`config set <key> <value>\` | Update config |
   268→| \`adapters\` | List adapters |
   269→| \`tunnel\` | Tunnel status |
   270→| \`notify "message"\` | Send notification |
   271→| \`version\` | Daemon version |
   272→| \`restart\` | Restart daemon |
   273→
   274→---
   275→
   276→## File Viewer (Tunnel)
   277→
   278→When tunnel is enabled, file edits and diffs get "View" buttons that open in your browser:
   279→- **Monaco Editor** — Full VS Code editor with syntax highlighting
   280→- **Diff viewer** — Side-by-side or inline comparison
   281→- **Line highlighting** — Click lines to highlight
   282→- Dark/light theme toggle
   283→
   284→### Setup
   285→Enable in config: set \`tunnel.enabled\` to \`true\`.
   286→Providers: Cloudflare (default, free), ngrok, bore, Tailscale Funnel.
   287→
   288→### Port Tunneling
   289→
   290→Expose any local port (dev servers, APIs, etc.) to the internet:
   291→
   292→**CLI commands** (agent can call these directly):
   293→- \`openacp tunnel add <port> --label <name>\` — Create tunnel to a local port
   294→- \`openacp tunnel list\` — List active tunnels
   295→- \`openacp tunnel stop <port>\` — Stop a tunnel
   296→- \`openacp tunnel stop-all\` — Stop all user tunnels
   297→
   298→**Telegram commands**:
   299→- \`/tunnel <port> [label]\` — Create tunnel
   300→- \`/tunnels\` — List active tunnels
   301→- \`/tunnel stop <port>\` — Stop tunnel
   302→
   303→Example: after starting a dev server on port 3000, run \`openacp tunnel add 3000 --label my-app\` to get a public URL.
   304→
   305→---
   306→
   307→## Configuration
   308→
   309→Config file: \`~/.openacp/config.json\`
   310→
   311→### Channels
   312→- **channels.telegram.botToken** — Your Telegram bot token
   313→- **channels.telegram.chatId** — Your Telegram supergroup ID
   314→- **channels.discord.botToken** — Your Discord bot token
   315→- **channels.discord.guildId** — Your Discord server (guild) ID
   316→
   317→### Agents
   318→- **defaultAgent** — Which agent to use by default
   319→- Agents are managed via \`/agents\` (Telegram) or \`openacp agents\` (CLI)
   320→- Installed agents are stored in \`~/.openacp/agents.json\`
   321→- Agent list is fetched from the ACP Registry CDN and cached locally (24h)
   322→
   323→### Workspace
   324→- **workspace.baseDir** — Base directory for project folders (default: \`~/openacp-workspace\`)
   325→
   326→### Security
   327→- **security.allowedUserIds** — Restrict who can use the bot (empty = everyone)
   328→- **security.maxConcurrentSessions** — Max parallel sessions (default: 5)
   329→- **security.sessionTimeoutMinutes** — Auto-cancel idle sessions (default: 60)
   330→
   331→### Tunnel / File Viewer
   332→- **tunnel.enabled** — Enable file viewer tunnel
   333→- **tunnel.provider** — Tunnel provider: cloudflare (default, free), ngrok, bore, tailscale
   334→- **tunnel.port** — Local port for tunnel server (default: 3100)
   335→- **tunnel.auth.enabled** — Enable authentication for tunnel URLs
   336→- **tunnel.auth.token** — Auth token for tunnel access
   337→- **tunnel.storeTtlMinutes** — How long viewer links stay cached (default: 60)
   338→
   339→### Logging
   340→- **logging.level** — Log level: silent, debug, info, warn, error, fatal (default: info)
   341→- **logging.logDir** — Log directory (default: \`~/.openacp/logs\`)
   342→- **logging.maxFileSize** — Max log file size before rotation
   343→- **logging.maxFiles** — Max number of rotated log files
   344→- **logging.sessionLogRetentionDays** — Auto-delete old session logs (default: 30)
   345→
   346→### Data Retention
   347→- **sessionStore.ttlDays** — How long session records persist (default: 30). Old records are cleaned up automatically.
   348→
   349→### Environment variables
   350→Override config with env vars:
   351→- \`OPENACP_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN\`
   352→- \`OPENACP_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID\`
   353→- \`OPENACP_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN\`
   354→- \`OPENACP_DISCORD_GUILD_ID\`
   355→- \`OPENACP_DEFAULT_AGENT\`
   356→- \`OPENACP_RUN_MODE\` — foreground or daemon
   357→- \`OPENACP_API_PORT\` — API server port (default: 21420)
   358→- \`OPENACP_TUNNEL_ENABLED\`
   359→- \`OPENACP_TUNNEL_PORT\`
   360→- \`OPENACP_TUNNEL_PROVIDER\`
   361→- \`OPENACP_LOG_LEVEL\`
   362→- \`OPENACP_LOG_DIR\`
   363→- \`OPENACP_DEBUG\` — Sets log level to debug
   364→
   365→---
   366→
   367→## Troubleshooting
   368→
   369→### Session stuck / not responding
   370→- Check status: ask Assistant "Is anything stuck?"
   371→- Cancel and create new: \`/cancel\` then \`/new\`
   372→- Check system health: Assistant can run health check
   373→
   374→### Agent not found
   375→- Check available agents: \`/agents\` or \`openacp agents\`
   376→- Install missing agent: \`openacp agents install <name>\`
   377→- Some agents need login first: \`openacp agents info <name>\` to see setup steps
   378→- Run agent CLI for setup: \`openacp agents run <name> -- <args>\`
   379→
   380→### Permission request not showing
   381→- Check Notifications topic for the alert
   382→- Try \`/enable_dangerous\` to auto-approve (if you trust the agent)
   383→
   384→### Session disappeared after restart
   385→- Sessions persist across restarts
   386→- Send a message in the old topic — it auto-resumes
   387→- If topic was deleted, the session record may still exist in status
   388→
   389→### Bot not responding at all
   390→- Check daemon: \`openacp status\`
   391→- Check logs: \`openacp logs\`
   392→- Restart: \`openacp start\` or \`/restart\`
   393→
   394→### Messages going to wrong topic
   395→- Each session is bound to a specific topic/thread
   396→- If you see messages appearing in the Assistant topic instead of the session topic, try creating a new session
   397→
   398→### Viewing logs
   399→- Session-specific logs: \`~/.openacp/logs/sessions/\`
   400→- System logs: \`openacp logs\` to tail live
   401→- Set \`OPENACP_DEBUG=true\` for verbose output
   402→
   403→---
   404→
   405→## Data & Storage
   406→
   407→All data is stored in \`~/.openacp/\`:
   408→- \`config.json\` — Configuration
   409→- \`agents.json\` — Installed agents (managed by AgentCatalog)
   410→- \`registry-cache.json\` — Cached ACP Registry data (refreshes every 24h)
   411→- \`agents/\` — Downloaded binary agents
   412→- \`sessions/\` — Session records and state
   413→- \`topics/\` — Topic-to-session mappings
   414→- \`logs/\` — System and session logs
   415→- \`plugins/\` — Installed adapter plugins
   416→- \`openacp.pid\` — Daemon PID file
   417→
   418→Session records auto-cleanup: 30 days (configurable via \`sessionStore.ttlDays\`).
   419→Session logs auto-cleanup: 30 days (configurable via \`logging.sessionLogRetentionDays\`).
   420→`;
   421→

# Extract Discord Plugin Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Extract the Discord adapter from OpenACP's built-in plugins into a standalone npm package `@openacp/plugin-discord`.

**Architecture:** Copy all 29 files from `src/plugins/discord/` to the standalone repo at `/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/discord-plugin/`. Extend `@openacp/plugin-sdk` to re-export all symbols the Discord plugin needs. Replace all `../../core/` imports with `@openacp/plugin-sdk`. Remove Discord from OpenACP's built-in plugins.

**Tech Stack:** TypeScript, ESM, vitest, discord.js ^14.x, @openacp/plugin-sdk

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-27-extract-discord-plugin-design.md`

---

## File Structure

### OpenACP repo changes:
- Modify: `packages/plugin-sdk/src/index.ts` — add ~20 re-exports
- Modify: `packages/plugin-sdk/src/testing.ts` — add `runAdapterConformanceTests` re-export
- Modify: `src/core/adapter-primitives/index.ts` — export format-utils and message-formatter
- Modify: `src/core/index.ts` — export CommandRegistry, DoctorEngine, PRODUCT_GUIDE, etc.
- Modify: `src/core/plugin/lifecycle-manager.ts` — add migration alias
- Modify: `src/plugins/core-plugins.ts` — remove Discord
- Delete: `src/plugins/discord/` — entire directory
- Modify: `package.json` — remove discord.js dependency

### New discord-plugin repo:
- Create: `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `.gitignore`, `.npmignore`
- Create: `src/index.ts` — refactored plugin entry
- Copy+refactor: all 26 source files from `src/plugins/discord/`
- Copy+refactor: all 3 test files from `src/plugins/discord/__tests__/`

---

### Task 1: Extend @openacp/cli exports

Add missing symbols to the CLI's public API so the Plugin SDK can re-export them.

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/core/adapter-primitives/index.ts`
- Modify: `src/core/index.ts`
- Modify: `src/index.ts`

- [ ] **Step 1: Add format-utils and message-formatter exports to adapter-primitives/index.ts**

```typescript

```

- [ ] **Step 2: Add CommandRegistry, Doctor, PRODUCT_GUIDE exports to core/index.ts**

```typescript

export type { DoctorReport, PendingFix } from './doctor/types.js'

```

- [ ] **Step 3: Verify build passes**

Run: `pnpm build`
Expected: No errors

- [ ] **Step 4: Commit**

```bash
git add src/core/adapter-primitives/index.ts src/core/index.ts
git commit -m "feat(core): export format-utils, message-formatter, CommandRegistry, Doctor, PRODUCT_GUIDE for plugin SDK"
```

1→# Extract Discord Plugin to Standalone Package
     2→
     3→## Problem
     4→
     5→The Discord adapter is bundled as a built-in plugin in OpenACP, meaning `discord.js` and its dependencies are installed for all users even if they don't use Discord. This adds unnecessary weight. The plugin should be a separate package that users install only when needed.
     6→
     7→## Solution
     8→
     9→Extract `src/plugins/discord/` from the OpenACP monorepo into a standalone package `@openacp/plugin-discord` in a separate repository. Extend `@openacp/plugin-sdk` to export all types/classes the Discord plugin needs. Remove the Discord plugin from the OpenACP repo.
    10→
    11→## Target Repository
    12→
    13→`/Users/lab3/Documents/lab3/discord-plugin/` → published as `@openacp/plugin-discord` on npm.
    14→
    15→**Note on naming:** The current built-in plugin is named `@openacp/discord`. The extracted plugin will be renamed to `@openacp/plugin-discord`. The legacy migration map in `lifecycle-manager.ts` (`'@openacp/discord': 'channels.discord'`) must be updated to also match the new name to preserve backward compatibility for config migration.
    16→
    17→## Standalone Plugin Structure
    18→
    19→```
    20→discord-plugin/
    21→  src/
    22→    index.ts                    # Plugin entry (OpenACPPlugin interface)
    23→    adapter.ts                  # DiscordAdapter (extends MessagingAdapter)
    24→    renderer.ts                 # Discord-specific message rendering
    25→    formatting.ts               # Markdown formatting for Discord
    26→    streaming.ts                # Message streaming/chunking
    27→    draft-manager.ts            # Draft message management
    28→    tool-call-tracker.ts        # Tool call display
    29→    skill-command-manager.ts    # Skill command UI
    30→    activity.ts                 # Activity indicators
    31→    permissions.ts              # Permission request buttons
    32→    forums.ts                   # Forum channel management
    33→    assistant.ts                # Assistant topic handler
    34→    action-detect.ts            # Action detection
    35→    media.ts                    # Media/file handling
    36→    types.ts                    # Discord-specific types
    37→    validators.ts               # Config validation
    38→    commands/
    39→      index.ts
    40→      admin.ts
    41→      agents.ts
    42→      doctor.ts
    43→      integrate.ts
    44→      menu.ts
    45→      new-session.ts
    46→      router.ts
    47→      session.ts
    48→      settings.ts
    49→    __tests__/
    50→      conformance.test.ts
    51→      formatting.test.ts
    52→      media.test.ts
    53→  package.json
    54→  tsconfig.json
    55→  .gitignore
    56→  .npmignore
    57→  README.md
    58→```
    59→
    60→### `package.json`
    61→
    62→```json
    63→{
    64→  "name": "@openacp/plugin-discord",
    65→  "version": "0.1.0",
    66→  "type": "module",
    67→  "main": "dist/index.js",
    68→  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
    69→  "exports": {
    70→    ".": {
    71→      "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
    72→      "import": "./dist/index.js"
    73→    }
    74→  },
    75→  "scripts": {
    76→    "build": "tsc",
    77→    "dev": "tsc --watch",
    78→    "test": "vitest",
    79→    "prepublishOnly": "npm run build"
    80→  },
    81→  "peerDependencies": {
    82→    "@openacp/plugin-sdk": ">=2026.0326.0"
    83→  },
    84→  "dependencies": {
    85→    "discord.js": "^14.x"
    86→  },
    87→  "devDependencies": {
    88→    "@openacp/plugin-sdk": ">=2026.0326.0",
    89→    "typescript": "^5.4.0",
    90→    "vitest": "^3.0.0"
    91→  }
    92→}
    93→```
    94→
    95→### `tsconfig.json`
    96→
    97→```json
    98→{
    99→  "compilerOptions": {
   100→    "target": "ES2022",
   101→    "module": "NodeNext",
   102→    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
   103→    "declaration": true,
   104→    "outDir": "dist",
   105→    "rootDir": "src",
   106→    "strict": true,
   107→    "esModuleInterop": true,
   108→    "skipLibCheck": true,
   109→    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true
   110→  },
   111→  "include": ["src"],
   112→  "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist"]
   113→}
   114→```
   115→
   116→## Import Migration
   117→
   118→All `../../core/` imports in the Discord plugin will be replaced with imports from `@openacp/plugin-sdk`.
   119→
   120→### Already exported by Plugin SDK (no SDK changes needed)
   121→
   122→- Plugin interfaces: `OpenACPPlugin`, `PluginContext`, `InstallContext`, `CommandDef`, `CommandResponse`, `MenuOption`, `ListItem`
   123→- Service interfaces: `SecurityService`, `FileServiceInterface`, `NotificationService`, `UsageService`, `SpeechServiceInterface`, `TunnelServiceInterface`, `ContextService`
   124→- Adapter base classes: `MessagingAdapter`, `StreamAdapter`, `BaseRenderer`
   125→- Adapter primitives: `SendQueue`, `DraftManager`, `ToolCallTracker`, `ActivityTracker`
   126→
   127→### Need to add to Plugin SDK
   128→
   129→These are currently internal to `@openacp/cli` and need to be re-exported from `@openacp/plugin-sdk`:
   130→
   131→**Adapter types (currently not re-exported despite being used by adapters):**
   132→- `IChannelAdapter`, `AdapterCapabilities`
   133→- `OutgoingMessage`, `PermissionRequest`, `NotificationMessage`, `AgentCommand`
   134→- `IRenderer`, `RenderedMessage`
   135→
   136→**Format types:**
   137→- `DisplayVerbosity`, `ToolCallMeta`, `ToolUpdateMeta`, `ViewerLinks`, `STATUS_ICONS`, `KIND_ICONS`
   138→
   139→**Format utilities:**
   140→- `progressBar`, `formatTokens`, `truncateContent`, `stripCodeFences`, `splitMessage`
   141→
   142→**Message formatter:**
   143→- `extractContentText`, `formatToolSummary`, `formatToolTitle`, `resolveToolIcon`
   144→
   145→**Core classes:**
   146→- `OpenACPCore` — needed by adapter to access core methods
   147→- `Session` — needed for session interaction
   148→- `SessionManager` — needed for session lookup
   149→- `CommandRegistry` — needed for command routing
   150→- `AgentCatalog` — accessed via `core.agentCatalog`
   151→
   152→**Doctor system:**
   153→- `DoctorEngine`, `DoctorReport`, `PendingFix` — needed for `/doctor` command
   154→
   155→**Config utilities:**
   156→- `ConfigFieldDef`, `getSafeFields`, `resolveOptions`, `getConfigValue`, `isHotReloadable` — needed for `/settings` command
   157→- `ConfigManager` (or its `save()` parameter type) — accessed via `core.configManager`
   158→
   159→**Core methods accessed on OpenACPCore:**
   160→- `requestRestart` — accessed by admin commands
   161→
   162→**Types:**
   163→- `SessionStatus`, `ConfigOption`, `UsageRecord`, `UsageSummary`, `PlanEntry`, `Attachment`, `StopReason`, `DiscordPlatformData`, `InstallProgress`
   164→
   165→**Data:**
   166→- `PRODUCT_GUIDE` — product guide text used in assistant topic. Must first be exported from `@openacp/cli`'s public API surface (`src/core/index.ts`), then re-exported from SDK.
   167→
   168→## Plugin Metadata
   169→
   170→The extracted plugin should set:
   171→- `name: '@openacp/plugin-discord'`
   172→- `essential: false` — since it's an optional plugin users choose to install
   173→- `pluginDependencies`: references `@openacp/security` and `@openacp/notifications` by their built-in names. The lifecycle manager resolves these by matching against loaded plugin names. Built-in plugins load before external plugins, so these dependencies will always be available when the Discord plugin loads.
   174→
   175→## Changes to OpenACP Repo
   176→
   177→### Remove from OpenACP
   178→
   179→1. Delete `src/plugins/discord/` entirely
   180→2. Remove Discord registration from `src/plugins/core-plugins.ts`
   181→3. Remove `discord.js` from `package.json` dependencies
   182→
   183→### Extend Plugin SDK
   184→
   185→Add all missing re-exports listed above to `packages/plugin-sdk/src/index.ts`. All re-exports come from `@openacp/cli` — the SDK is a thin re-export layer, no new code.
   186→
   187→### Update legacy migration map
   188→
   189→In `src/core/plugin/lifecycle-manager.ts`, add `'@openacp/plugin-discord'` as an alias mapping to `'channels.discord'` alongside the existing `'@openacp/discord'` entry. This ensures config migration works for both the old built-in name and the new package name.
   190→
   191→### No changes needed
   192→
   193→- Core plugin loader works as-is for external plugins
   194→- Config schema, session management, adapter interface unchanged
   195→- `openacp plugin add` command handles npm install of plugin + its dependencies
   196→
   197→## User Installation Flow
   198→
   199→```bash
   200→# Install from npm (after publishing)
   201→openacp plugin add @openacp/plugin-discord
   202→
   203→# Install from local path (development)
   204→openacp plugin add /path/to/discord-plugin
   205→
   206→# Development with hot-reload
   207→openacp dev /path/to/discord-plugin
   208→
   209→# Uninstall
   210→openacp plugin remove @openacp/plugin-discord
   211→```
   212→
   213→When installed, `discord.js` is npm-installed as a dependency of the plugin. When not installed, OpenACP has zero Discord-related dependencies.
   214→
   215→## Testing
   216→
   217→### Standalone repo tests
   218→
   219→- **Conformance test**: `runAdapterConformanceTests` must be added to `@openacp/plugin-sdk/testing` exports (currently only in `src/core/adapter-primitives/__tests__/adapter-conformance.ts`). Add it as a re-export from the SDK testing entry point.
   220→- **Unit tests**: Copy existing formatting.test.ts, media.test.ts from OpenACP
   221→- **Dev mode**: `openacp dev .` in the plugin directory for hot-reload testing
   222→
   223→### Edge cases
   224→
   225→- Plugin installed but Discord bot token not configured: plugin's `install()` should prompt for token
   226→- Plugin removed while Discord sessions active: graceful shutdown of Discord adapter
   227→- SDK version mismatch: peerDependency warning from npm
   228→- Boot order: built-in service plugins (@openacp/security, @openacp/notifications) must load before external plugins to satisfy `pluginDependencies`
   229→
   230→## Files Modified (Summary)
   231→
   232→### OpenACP repo
   233→- `packages/plugin-sdk/src/index.ts` — Add ~40 re-exports
   234→- `packages/plugin-sdk/src/testing.ts` — Add `runAdapterConformanceTests` re-export
   235→- `src/core/plugin/lifecycle-manager.ts` — Add `@openacp/plugin-discord` to migration map
   236→- `src/plugins/core-plugins.ts` — Remove Discord registration
   237→- `src/plugins/discord/` — Delete entirely
   238→- `package.json` — Remove `discord.js` dependency
   239→
   240→### New discord-plugin repo
   241→- All 29 files from `src/plugins/discord/` copied and refactored
   242→- New `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `.gitignore`, `.npmignore`, `README.md`
   243→- All `../../core/` imports replaced with `@openacp/plugin-sdk`
   244→
